At least one person was injured when a heavy light fixture fell into the crowd during John Summit’s surprise Friday night DJ set at Coachella’s Do LaB stage, according to onlookers. Witnesses said festivalgoers carried the injured attendee out of the crowd for medical attention as strong winds disrupted the festival.

Today, the local mini chain with stores in Fremont, Sunnyvale and Union City is primarily run by his sons, Rajan and Sandeep Birla. In the 1970 census, only 51,000 Indian-born people were recorded in the United States. “Back then, it was a very small community, so there wasn’t really a huge customer base to profit off of,” Rajan said. “But they took a risk, and it kind of grew with the population.” Read the full story at the link in comments.SFGATE1.8K views · 1h ago2:00“If you like Indian food, you’re going to like Burmese food. If you like Chinese food, you’ll like Burmese food too,” says Chef Ron Chu, who runs the Burma Love downtown kitchen in San Francisco. Since opening in the Mission in 2014 as an offshoot of the beloved Burma Superstar in the Richmond, Burma Love has grown to five Bay Area locations. And in a city that’s famously just seven by seven miles, San Francisco now has more than a dozen Burmese restaurants. The fandom for Burma Love is clear: SFGATE readers voted it the Best Burmese Restaurant in the Bay last year in our annual Best of the Bay Area readers’ choice awards (humorously, Burma Superstar came in second place). SFGATE’s Melissa Cho recently stopped by the downtown location to find out what keeps diners coming back. Voting for this year’s Best of the Bay Area starts today. At the Masonic last Thursday night, the crowd of mostly twenty-somethings joined together in a four-syllable chant: “Ta-ka-na-ka.” A few seconds later, the 73-year-old Japanese musician stepped on stage wearing a bright red suit and black bow tie, and the crowd erupted in a cheer so loud it left SFGATE senior culture editor Dan Gentile's ears ringing later that night. Read the full review at the link in comments.SFGATE8.8K views · 1d ago0:14BigBang knows how to make an entrance. They wasted no time during their Sunday night Coachella performance, starting with one of their biggest hits, “Bang Bang Bang.” It was an explosive start to BigBang’s set, and fitting for the occasion. The group’s performance was a special treat for K-pop fans. BigBang went on hiatus for mandatory military service at the end of the 2010s, hasn’t released new music since 2022 and hasn’t toured since 2017. Within the K-pop genre, BigBang remains enormously influential. The members of BTS cite BigBang as one of their primary inspirations. “It wouldn’t be an exaggeration to say that BigBang practically made BTS,” Suga, a BTS member, once told Taeyang, a member of BigBang. “You were musicians that I aspired to be like as a kid.” Read the full review at the link in comments.SFGATE56.2K views · 2d ago0:19Behind Karol G, Young Thug, the Atlanta rapper, was the top-billed Coachella act on Sunday. That placement was the culmination of a decade-plus career, spanning a dizzying number of mixtapes and now-classic hooks. Thug, whose vocal contortions echo in the raps of Playboi Carti, Lil Baby and countless others, is probably one of the most influential rappers of his generation. The performance is part of an extended victory lap for the rapper, following a string of smaller festival appearances in 2025. In October 2024, the rapper was released from jail in Fulton County, Georgia, after spending two years tied up in the longest trial in the state’s history. Read the full review at the link in comments.SFGATE5.9K views · 2d ago0:19On Sunday night, Karol G became the first Latina to ever headline Coachella — a feat she acknowledged with a swell of pride, and disbelief, during a poignant moment in her set. “I’m very happy and very proud about this, but at the same time, it feels late,” she told the crowd, noting that she wouldn’t be up there were it not for the Latino artists that had come before her, who hadn’t been afforded the same opportunity. To close out Coachella, the musician turned out a high-octane performance that erupted into the biggest party of the weekend. In a breakneck, 25-song set that elevated divergent styles under the vast umbrella of Latin music, including reggaeton, mariachi and merengue, she intentionally kept the door open behind her so others could walk through it. In the past year, the TikToker-slash-dancer has had one of pop music’s more fascinating and controversial arcs. Her slow-burn Coachella entrance felt telling: Saturday evening’s main stage set was the last brief moment before yet another pivotal turn. Read the full review at the link in comments.SFGATE15.7K views · 2d ago0:37Three years after retreating from the spotlight, Justin Bieber's Saturday night headlining Coachella set was supposed to be his biggest performance in years. What fans hoped for, it seems, was vintage Bieber. They wanted the hits: “Baby,” “One Less Lonely Girl,” “Sorry.” They wanted nostalgia; they wanted a dance party. Bieber had other ideas. Things got weird a third of the way through the set when Bieber started playing through his old material. Or rather, his computer did. The singer sat perched in front of his Mac, searching for his old music videos on YouTube. He shared his computer’s screen so that the crowd could see.
